pr_title: sql: reduce memory usage of activity update job
pr_body:
Problem:
The `array_agg` was causing a large amount of memory.

Solution:
This adds 3 new aggregate functions to avoid `array_agg` .
The functions are `merge_stats_metadata` ,`merge_statement_stats` ,
`merge_transaction_stats`. They only create a single object and keep
adding to the single object instead of allocating an array of all the JSON 
objects and then passing it to a function to aggregate. The new functions
are undocumented to avoid customers from taking a dependency on 
this logic.

Fixes: #111866

Release note (sql change): Reduces the sql activity job memory usage.

issue_context.title: sql: activity update job reduce memory usage
issue_context.body:
The activity update job query can cause very large arrays to be created with the `array_agg`. There are some statements that have over 9k+ rows which can consume a lot of memory.  This can be optimized with a new function which aggregates the data into a single instance and avoid the need for converting it to an array.

Jira issue: CRDB-32104

review_comments: More for my own understanding again, why do we not update memory usage while in the helper functions? Is the idea that we're only creating a single object per helper function call which subsequently gets garbage collected?
